enemies.grid_notes: GOÐI ÞORGEIR (Rename Table; C-DAG-01, Y-6 presider). Presides the rite before the pyre at [11,1], the white bull led beneath the hanging-tree at [13,1]. NEVER engages and is never targetable: the 3h scarp (row 3 ditch, elev 1, under the elev-4 terrace), the elev-7 crag shoulders flanking the terrace, and script keep him out of reach. Withdraws N with the rite-guard when three wardens fall. His presence is the battle's moral architecture, not its difficulty.
Rite-guard on the terrace lip at the goat-track top ([8,3]->[8,2], the only sub-2h ascent). Fighting him is optional; the objective is on the road below.

Warden on the mid-rise, elev 2 — standing in one of the two tree-line windows ([9,4]/[12,4]) that see the terrace. Hunts the travelers: prioritizes downing civilians over engaging soldiers. The AI cruelty that makes the escort real.
Warden on the west road behind the travelers; drives the flock from behind, forcing pace.

Bow on the east tree-line, elev 3: kill-lane covers the road's east exit (cols 16-17, rows 6-7, 2h advantage = +1 range). The player must climb INTO witness-height (elev 2-3, rows 3-5) to silence him — clearing the safe road creates the seeing ground.
The wardens' blunt instrument, planted mid-road facing the oncoming flock; goes for whoever guards the travelers. (Brief facing SE is not in the facing enum; W faces the approaching escort.)
Rite-sister on the terrace lip west; chants ward-verses (buffs wardens' resolve) from elev 4; retreats with Þorgeir. Downing her requires the goat-track — again, at witness-height.

neutrals.grid_notes: Freed thrall, manumission-cord at his wrist; leads the group east along the road at 3-move.
His wife; stays within 1 tile of n1 or stalls.
Old freedman, 2-move — the pace-setter the wardens count on catching.

Young freedwoman on the south verge; PANICS toward high ground when a warden closes — likeliest to climb uncommanded onto the elev-2 rise base (row 5) and through a sightline window ([9,5]/[12,5]). The gimmick's live wire.

Charcoal-burner already ON the rise (elev 3, beside the goat-track bend) when battle starts — already sighted on the terrace lip and the rite spilling across it. He flees WEST along the rise, away from the group: the player must choose whether to spend turns on him at all.

objectives.primary: See the travelers through: at least three of n1-n4 exit the east edge.
secondary: n4 exits without ever standing on elevation 2+ (the quiet road — protects HER from what seeing costs).
No warden routs north to the terrace (the grove never learns exactly who fought for the witnesses).
objectives.defeat: Grím falls, or all of n1-n4 are downed.

triggers.note: The rite crests: from any elev 2+ tile with clear LoS the terrace becomes readable testimony (pyre stacked, white bull led out, Þorgeir's silhouette against the hanging-tree). Post-battle script writes the enum: 'talked' if any neutral escaped after holding sightline, 'unseen' if neutrals escaped but none ever saw, 'silenced' if every sighted unit died. Read by scene ch1-s06.

Remaining wardens rout N up the goat-track ([7,5]->[8,4]->[8,3]->[8,2]); Þorgeir's withdrawal begins. N is an escape edge: wardens who exit it count as routers escaping under C-ALIGN-04 — the battle can be Sung by their flight alone, which is thematically right: fleeing wardens TALK. (The secondary objective asks the player to deny them exactly that.)
Þorgeir studies the masked boy from the terrace lip a long moment — recognition without name. Seeds Ch2/Ch3 (his dossier's 'may glimpse').
Under the grove's eyes the VFX reads as doctrine CONFIRMED — the wardens cry out in vindication. The Lie flexing (C-LIE-01).

designer_notes.height_gimmick: Sightline as testimony: the blót terrace (rows 0-2, cols 8-14, elev 4, dead level) is visible ONLY from tiles of elevation 2+ with clear LoS past the tree-rocks (free-standing rock-and-tree tiles at [2,3],[5,3],[2,4],[6,4],[10,4],[14,4], raised to elev 6 — ~3h above their neighbors — so that under D-TERR-02's passable-rock ruling they still block movement and LoS by height alone, C-ELEV-02) — C-ELEV-01's LoS rule reused for witnessing, not damage. From the road (rows 6-7, elev 0-1) the rise band (rows 4-5, every terrace-facing column holding elev 2-3) sits at/above the sightline, so civilians herded along the low road see nothing and can swear to nothing; two windows in the tree-line (cols 9 and 12, where row 4 dips to elev 2) let elev-2 tiles at [9,4]/[12,4]/[9,5]/[12,5] see the altar. Physical access is separately throttled: the scarp-foot ditch (row 3, cols 9-14, elev 1) makes the terrace front a Jump-proof 3h sheer, and the elev-7 crag shoulders (rows 0-2, cols 0-7 and 15-17) wall off both flanks — necessary because rock is passable stone under D-TERR-02, so only elevation deltas bar the way; the sole route onto the elev-4 terrace is the goat-track [7,5]->[8,4]->[8,3]->[8,2], all 1h steps (C-ELEV-02) — the rite is architecturally out of the player's reach except through its one guarded gate. The only Ch1 map where elevation decides not what you can HIT but what can be SUNG.
designer_notes.witness_setup: Five travelers flee while grove-wardens hunt them — the wardens' whole objective is preventing witnesses to a present-day, post-ban, ILLEGAL blót (Y0, C-WORLD-05/OQ-5). Escorts n1-n3 start on the west road (elev 0-1, blind), n4 on the south verge and prone to panic-climbing into sightline, n5 already on the rise at [7,3] (elev 3, already sighted) fleeing W away from the group. The player chooses what the survivors saw: shepherd them low and fast (escape, but unseen — they can only attest a skirmish), let or help them reach elev 2+ (escape as true blót-witnesses — they will TALK, grove_blot_witnessed='talked'), or fail/silence every sighted unit ('silenced'). Þorgeir is present, presiding, and untouchable; preventing testimony is fully possible and fully remembered (C-ALIGN-03).
designer_notes.intent: Escort mission and the witness-system masterclass — the Sung/Unsung lesson taught with civilians who flee and TALK. Faith-nuance carried in both hands: the travelers are freed thralls walking to the coast under manumission-cords (the new faith's genuine gift, C-LIE-04), and the rite on the terrace is the old faith's real belonging curdled into desperation (C-LIE-05/05a) — Þorgeir sacrifices a WHITE BULL, not a person, this time; the escalation is dread, not gore (C-TONE-04). Hallowed overlay on the terrace unsettles old-faith levy units who reach it via the goat-track — texture, not hazard. No fire event exists on this map: the pyre stays flammable-but-unlit so it cannot become ch1-08's rhyme too early.
